newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka cuts banks' reserve requirement to 12%.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka cuts banks' reserve requirement to 12%.

text.p: Sri Lanka's Central Bank said on Monday it was cutting its reserve requirements in a move to ease monetary policy.
"We have cut the reserve requirement for banks to 12 percent from 14 with immediate effect," Central Bank Governor A.S. Jayawardene told Reuters.
The Central Bank last cut the reserve requirement in January when it lowered it to 14 percent from an earlier 15 percent. It also permitted exporters to borrow in foreign currency.
That led call money rates to drop to an average 12 percent from around 15 percent.
Jayawardene said the latest cut in banks' reserve requirement will release 5.3 billion rupees into the system, helping interest rates to fall below the current level of around 10 percent.
"Since the incremental inflation in the last five months has been three percent we are comfortable with the move," he said.
Annualised inlfation was 16.7 percent in February.
